keyFindings.description: The failed-hand-back restore loop, returned to its unconditional form this round, is not bounded to a redundant soft claim. That bound is the reviewer's own round-4 audit and it was wrong; this finding corrects it. Path A, the one that takes a role: a loop under host A removes `X@A`, its unsubscribe fails so the entry lives only in the local `failed` array, and the task is abandoned at its deadline. The process moves to B, which claims X successfully - that claim clears pendingHandBacks and abandonedHolds of X (:1938-1941) but cannot reach the old loop's local array. Another process resumes A and claims X, so A is the newer live holder. The old loop then finishes and restores `X@A` into pendingHandBacks, because its captured `host` is still A. B's next pass wants X, adopts that entry over its own confirmed state (:2281-2285, setting claimedRoleSessionID = A and holdUnconfirmed = true), computes supersedes = A (:2366) and sends the soft claim with previousSessionID = A (:2384). The listener supersedes a holder that matches previous_session_id even when that holder is live - packages/envoy/cmd/listener/api.go:822-825, 'so may the claimant's own predecessor, live or not', applied at packages/envoy/internal/store/kv.go:612-615 - so B takes X from the process now running A, and that role's traffic follows B. Without the resurrected entry B's pass would have soft-claimed with no predecessor, taken the 409 and relinquished (:1658-1693). Path B, underneath it: the loop classifies with the captured `host`, so a hold under a session the process has left since is filed as pending rather than abandoned. That is exactly the case settleEndedHolds' own comment says must go to abandonedHolds, 'since nothing heartbeats that session any more and a later try could take a hold another process made under that id' - the hazard Path A realises, named in the function and defeated by the stale capture. Round 5's topic-only skip blocked Path A while breaking the unconfirmed-adoption case; the revert restores Path A. Two conditions, wrong in opposite directions. `topic === claimedRoleTopic && !holdUnconfirmed` closes Path A and keeps round 5's case fixed, and classifying against the live host rather than the captured one closes Path B - but the reviewer does not assert that pair is sufficient, having now been wrong about this loop once, and the choice between a third targeted condition and a scoped redesign is the architect's.
